findings: Augmentation removal improves first-pair baseline at both dropout settings by3.52and4.65pp. Removing dropout alone reduces its baseline by0.93pp.
Five of six changed-base constraint candidates improve their own first-pair controls; plain bands is down0.022pp and rejected under the predeclared strict rule.
Noaug and plain constrained models improve absolute Dice strongly on this pair. Nodrop constrained models improve a weaker control but remain below the old absolute baseline.
Saved eval-mode logit probes show modest late changes in the band/base gradient ratio, not a monotonic relation with validation gain. They are not actual Adam-update measurements.
Noaug baseline on seed0fold2 is76.160558173 versus old70.137516551; its constraint comparisons are still running.
caveats: One completed factorial development pair; two noaug baselines. Consistency across9pairs is not established.
Macro gains need not improve every subfield; retain class-specific effects. A smaller train/validation gap was not associated with the better absolute baseline in the first pair.
Results concern this409-update53.305Tcap; do not infer that augmentation is generally harmful at longer budgets.
